maria: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection heuristic rollout (v2) landed last night, I'm seeing a ~12% increase in host-side parse/tokenize tail (P95) on the rtx-pool. Root cause looks like more time in the ingress framing path (http/gRPC decode) and `tokenize_async` stacks.

aj: Do you have a flame/pprof snapshot or perf script output we can look at?

maria: Pasted the top lines from a 30s pprof sample:
```
parse_stream::read_loop +38%
  ├─ http2::decode_headers +22%
  └─ tokenize_async +18%
syscalls: readv spikes on small frames (4-32B)
```
KV cache miss rate is flat, so it's not kvcache churn. The interesting bit: request batching sizes dropped (median batch size went from 6→3) after the selector started preferring the new `vec` kernel for short sequences. Fewer requests per batch -> more fragmented chunks over gRPC.

sasha: @maria can you paste the exact kernel selector config that rolled? Also which release tag?

maria: It was `kernel-selector: prefer_vec_for_len_lt=64, score=+0.2` rolled in `canary-2026-03-22`. I grabbed a short grep of traces showing repeated small `writev`/`readv` pairs and ~3x more syscall wakeups per token.

```bash
# quick repro capture command we ran
sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30
# then perf script | stackcollapse | flamegraph.pl
```

dennis: That matches my theory — the vec kernel reduced GPU decode time but its micro-batching behavior is less tolerant to host-side batching heuristics. When the runtime switches kernel, it also nudges the batching window smaller (to avoid head-of-line stalls), which in turn increases small-frame churn on ingress. Net effect: GPU time down but host tail up.

aj: Can we run a canary forcing the legacy kernel selection and measure end-to-end? e.g. `REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy ./run_canary.sh --pool rtx-2` then capture p95 and syscall counts. If we get p95 down, we know it's selector↔batching interaction.

perf-bot: Canary started: id=canary-1898765432-01, collecting 10k traces, sample interval=5s. Results will post to /tmp/canary-results.

maria: Kicking off the canary now. If this reproduces, short-term mitigation is to add a host-side guard: when ingress small-write rate > threshold, prefer legacy selector or bump batching timeout to favor larger bundles. I'll post p95 diffs when perf-bot finishes.

aj: Also add a lightweight metric: `host_small_write_rate` and tie it to the routing policy so we can auto-fallback. Small metric + cheap guard will avoid an SLA blip. :+1:

maria: Agreed. I'll open a quick PR with the metric and a fallback knob (opt-in) and attach the canary numbers. Thanks all.
